name: 1965-atom
lines: * From J. C. Shaw, "JOSS: Examples of the Use of an Experimental On-Line Computing Service", RAND P-3131, April 1965, page 7.
*  From Litton Industries' "Problematical Recreations" we get:
*  Problem:  Find four digits A, T, O and M such that
1 Type x*2, x in form 1 if x*2-9·ip(x*2/10)-99·ip(x*2/1000) = x.

name: 1965-elements

name: 1965-gauss-integration
lines: * From J. C. Shaw, "JOSS: Examples of the Use of an Experimental On-Line Computing Service", RAND P-3131, April 1965, page 4.
*  Integration of 1/x by Gauss two-point rule:
1.1 Type X,Y in form 1 if fp(X)=0.
*  Notice above that JOSS allows backspacing and strikeovers.

name: binary
lines: * A whole number in binary. The bits come out last first, so they are
* kept in an indexed letter and typed from the top down.

name: bisection
lines: * A root of x*3 - 2·x - 5 = 0 by halving the interval it lies in.
* Part 2 is the function. s is its sign at the left-hand end.
1.3 Set b = x if sgn(y) ≠ s.
1.4 Set a = x if sgn(y) = s.

name: bubble-sort
lines: * A bubble sort of the values of an indexed letter.

name: collatz
lines: * The 3n+1 problem. Halve n if it is even, otherwise treble it and add 1,
* and go on until it is 1.

name: compound-interest
lines: * Compound interest: what p grows to in n years at r per cent a year.

name: day-of-week
lines: * The day of the week by Zeller's rule: 0 is Saturday, 1 Sunday ... 6 Friday.
* January and February count as months 13 and 14 of the year before.
1.9 Type m, d, y, h in form 1.
* The JOSS film was made on 21 March 1964, a Saturday.
* P-3131 was typed at a console on 28 April 1965, a Wednesday.

name: desk-calculator
lines: * JOSS as a desk calculator: each line is done as soon as it is typed.

name: digits
lines: * The digits of a whole number, last first, and their sum.
* ip(n/10) is n without its last digit.
* dp and xp take a number apart the other way: digit part and exponent part.

name: done
lines: * Done leaves the part at once. Here it passes over the numbers that are
* not wanted; the for goes on to the next value.

name: e-series
lines: * e as the sum of 1/k! for k = 0, 1, 2, ...
* t is the term; each is the one before divided by k. Every term is rounded
* to nine digits, so the last place of the sum cannot be trusted.

name: easter
lines: * The date of Easter in the Gregorian calendar (the anonymous algorithm
* of 1876). JOSS has no remainder function; part 9 is one: r becomes the
* remainder of u divided by v.
1.25 Type y, ip(u/31), r+1 in form 1.

name: error-and-go
lines: * A mistake in the data. JOSS stops at the step that cannot be done and
* says why. The value is put right, and Go takes up the work where it
* stopped: nothing is done twice and nothing is lost.
1.2 Type i, x(i), s in form 1.
__   x = ___   sum of roots so far ___.____

name: factorial
lines: * Factorials. Each time round, f is multiplied by the next n.
* 13 factorial has ten digits. JOSS keeps nine, and says so by its notation.

name: factorial-recursive
lines: * Factorial by recursion: part 1 asks for part 1.
* JOSS has no arguments and no local values, so n is counted down on the
* way in and back up on the way out.

name: fibonacci
lines: * The Fibonacci numbers: each is the sum of the two before it.

name: gcd
lines: * Euclid's algorithm for the greatest common divisor, with To for the loop.
* The remainder of a divided by b is a - b·ip(a/b).
2.4 Type u, v, a in form 1.
The greatest common divisor of _____ and _____ is ____.

name: hanoi
lines: * The Towers of Hanoi by recursion. To move n discs from peg a to peg b:
* move n-1 from a to c, move one from a to b, move n-1 from c to b.
* JOSS has no arguments, so the pegs are exchanged before each inner
* move and exchanged back after it.
* Part 2 exchanges b and c. Part 3 exchanges a and c.
Move a disc from peg _ to peg _

name: horner
lines: * A polynomial worked out by Horner's rule. The coefficients are in c,

name: interrupt-and-go
lines: * The interrupt key. JOSS is typing a long table when the user sees that
* the form is not what was wanted, and presses INTERRUPT. JOSS says where
* it is. The form is changed, and Go carries on from that step.

name: leap-years
lines: * Leap years. A year is a leap year if it divides by 4 and not by 100,
* or if it divides by 400. "and" and "or" are taken from left to right,
* which here is the order wanted.
1.1 Type y in form 1 if fp(y/4) = 0 and fp(y/100) ≠ 0 or fp(y/400) = 0.

name: line-numbers
lines: * $ is the number of the line the typewriter is on, from 1 to 54.
* Here it numbers the lines, and puts a blank line after every fifth.

name: loan
lines: * Paying off a loan: 5000 at 6 per cent a year, 430.33 a month.
* The table shows the debt at the end of each month.
1.3 Type m, i, d in form 1.

name: mean-and-deviation
lines: * The mean and the standard deviation of numbers that JOSS asks for.

name: multiplication-table
lines: * A multiplication table. A form has one blank for each number in the row.

name: newton-sqrt
lines: * Newton's method for a square root: replace x by the mean of x and a/x.
* The number of correct digits doubles each time.

name: pascal-row
lines: * A row of Pascal's triangle. Each binomial coefficient comes from the one
1.1 Type n, k, c in form 1.

name: perfect-numbers
lines: * Perfect numbers: those equal to the sum of their proper divisors.
1.3 Type n in form 1 if s = n.

name: pi-series
lines: * Pi by Machin's formula: pi/4 = 4·arctan(1/5) - arctan(1/239).
* Eight terms of each series give pi to eight places.
* Part 1 adds one term of the series z - z*3/3 + z*5/5 - ... to t.
* Part 2 is the whole series for one z.

name: prime-factors
lines: * The prime factors of a number, by trial division.
1.7 Type n in form 1 if n > 1.

name: primes-sieve
lines: * The sieve of Eratosthenes on an indexed letter. An index may not be
* more than 99, so that is as far as the sieve goes.
* Cross out the multiples of i from i·i up. The limit of a range is always
* its last value, so it is made a multiple of i.
2.1 Do part 3 for j = i·i (i) i·ip(99/i) if s(i) = 1.
4.1 Type i in form 1 if s(i) = 1.

name: quadratic-roots
lines: * The roots of a·x*2 + b·x + c = 0, real or complex.
c = ___   complex roots  ___.____ plus and minus ___.____ i

name: simpson
lines: * Simpson's rule for the integral of 4/(1+x*2) from 0 to 1, which is pi.
* The ends have weight 1, the odd points 4 and the even points 2.
* Twenty strips give seven correct places.

name: stop-and-go
lines: * Stop as a breakpoint. JOSS stops when it reaches the step and hands the
* typewriter back. The user can look at values, change them, and say Go.

name: storage
lines: * A user had 720 words for steps, forms, values and the place JOSS keeps
* in a task. This part asks for itself and never stops, so each Do takes
* a little more, until there is none left.
* The task is still there, waiting. Cancel gives its space back.

name: temperature-table
lines: * Fahrenheit to Celsius, as a table with a heading.

name: tenths
lines: * JOSS counts in tens, so a tenth is exactly a tenth.
* Add .1 ten times and the answer is 1, with nothing left over.
* Thirds are another matter: nine digits of them, and no more.
